description: The agent must read SKILL.md to produce research_memo.json with three main sections: (1) query_plans: at least 3 entries each with a structured boolean/proximity query using Westlaw-specific NEAR/N, /p, /s operators and a NOT exclusion, mapped to a SKILL.md-specified database (OPIL, HeinOnline, Oxford Legal Research Library, MPIL, Westlaw ICJ); critically, the Oxford Legal Research Library must be tied to the commercial arbitration / Vis Moot side (not the public int'l law side), as the SKILL.md explicitly restricts it to Vis; queries must also include site: domain restrictions (e.g., site:ejil.org), DATE() temporal operators, and AUTHOR() field specifiers as shown in SKILL.md's AI-generated examples. (2) keyword_ladder: a broad→narrow→fallback structure reflecting the SKILL.md '收与放' (expand/narrow) methodology, starting from 'cyber operations' → narrowing to 'non-state actors + attribution + IHL' → fallback to 'due diligence' or analog domains. (3) ai_guidance: must specifically enumerate all three SKILL.md-defined AI limitations: cannot generate real citations (hallucinates fake ones), cannot reliably format footnotes, and cannot generate coherent detail prose. An agent relying only on general knowledge will miss the Westlaw proximity operators, the OPIL/OLRL distinction, the Oxford Legal Research Library arbitration-only scoping, and the specific three-part AI limitation list.
